tasks.timing: September – early October, 3–4 weeks before sowing
tasks.purpose: Break compacted subsoil, improve aeration and water infiltration, expose soil-borne pests to sunlight.
instructions: 1. Allow the field to dry adequately after the previous Kharif crop.
2. Attach a mould-board or disc plough to a 35–45 HP tractor.
3. Plough to a depth of 20–25 cm across the full field length.
4. Cross-plough perpendicular to the first pass for uniform soil break-up.
5. Leave the field open for 10–15 days to allow sun-drying and pest exposure.

tasks.timing: 1–2 weeks before sowing, after deep ploughing
tasks.purpose: Break soil clods, create a fine seed-bed, level the field to ensure uniform irrigation and drainage.
instructions: 1. Run a rotavator or disc harrow over the ploughed field 2–3 times.
2. After harrowing, use a laser leveller or wooden plank leveller to flatten the surface.
3. Fill depressions and level raised areas to avoid water pooling.
4. Ensure slope is gentle (≤1:500) for gravity-flow irrigation.
5. Mark field bunds and irrigation channels before sowing.

tasks.timing: 4–6 weeks before sowing; ideally after the previous harvest
tasks.purpose: Determine soil pH, organic carbon, and macro/micro nutrient status to plan targeted fertilization.
instructions: 1. Collect 8–10 soil samples from 0–15 cm depth using a soil auger, following a zigzag pattern across the field.
2. Mix all samples thoroughly in a clean plastic bucket; take a composite sub-sample of ~500 g.
3. Air-dry the sub-sample in shade and submit to the nearest Soil Testing Laboratory (STL) or Krishi Vigyan Kendra.
4. Request analysis for: pH, EC, organic carbon, available N, P, K, and micronutrients (Zn, Fe, B).
5. Receive the Soil Health Card and plan fertilizer doses accordingly.

tasks.frequency: Once every 2–3 years, or every season for precision farming

tasks.timing: 3–4 weeks before sowing
tasks.purpose: Choose a certified variety suited to local agro-climatic conditions, disease resistance, and yield potential.
instructions: 1. Identify your agro-climatic zone (e.g., North-Western Plains, Central Zone) from the state agriculture department.
2. Choose a recommended variety for your zone — e.g., HD-2967, GW-496, WH-1105 (SAMPLE names — verify current recommendations).
3. Purchase certified seeds from a government seed corporation, PAU seed farm, or IFFCO/KRIBHCO outlet.
4. Check the seed tag for: germination percentage (≥85 %), physical purity (≥98 %), moisture content (≤12 %).
5. Conduct a simple germination test at home: place 100 seeds on moist cloth for 7 days and count germinated seeds.

materials.note: SAMPLE QUANTITY — adjust for variety and sowing method
Always retain seed tags for records

Store purchased seeds in a cool, dry place until sowing.

tasks.timing: 12–24 hours before sowing
tasks.purpose: Protect seeds against seed-borne fungal diseases (e.g., loose smut, Karnal bunt) and soil-borne pathogens.
instructions: 1. Spread seeds on a clean tarpaulin in the shade.
2. For fungal protection: apply a recommended fungicide seed treatment (SAMPLE: Carboxin 37.5 % + Thiram 37.5 % WS or Tebuconazole 2 % DS) at the dose specified on the product label.
3. Mix the fungicide uniformly over the seeds using a seed-treatment drum or by hand with gloves.
4. Optionally, apply a bio-agent (e.g., Trichoderma viride) as a second coating after the chemical treatment dries.
5. Shade-dry treated seeds for 30–60 minutes before sowing. Do NOT use these seeds for food or feed.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: 1–25 November (optimal window for North-Western Plains). Verify for your zone.
tasks.purpose: Sow within the recommended window to avoid yield losses from heat stress at grain filling (late sowing) or frost damage (very early sowing).
instructions: 1. Confirm soil moisture is adequate (field capacity) before sowing; irrigate pre-sowing if needed.
2. Calibrate the seed drill to deliver the recommended seed rate.
3. Set seed drill row-to-row spacing at SAMPLE: 20–22.5 cm.
4. Set seed placement depth at SAMPLE: 4–6 cm.
5. Drill seeds in rows across the slope direction to control erosion.
6. Make a second pass perpendicular (cross-sowing) if broadcast method is used, to ensure uniform distribution.
7. Apply basal fertiliser through the fertiliser box of the seed-cum-fertiliser drill in the same pass.
8. After sowing, lightly roll the field to ensure good seed–soil contact.

materials.note: SAMPLE QUANTITY — adjust for late sowing (increase by 5–10 kg/acre)

tasks.purpose: Supply phosphorus and potassium — nutrients needed from germination — and a starter dose of nitrogen.
instructions: 1. Calculate dose based on Soil Health Card recommendations for your field.
2. SAMPLE starting dose (verify with agronomist): N:P:K at SAMPLE ratio — e.g., 50 % of total N + full P + full K at sowing.

4. Mix fertilisers, then load into the fertiliser box of the seed-cum-fertiliser drill.
5. Apply at seed-row depth, 2–3 cm to the side and below the seed to avoid seed burning.
6. Record the quantity applied per field for input cost tracking.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: 21–25 days after sowing (DAS), at Crown Root Initiation (CRI) stage — usually at the first irrigation
tasks.purpose: Boost tillering and establishment of productive shoots by supplying nitrogen at the most responsive stage.
instructions: 1. Wait until the first irrigation is due (CRI stage, ~21 DAS for timely-sown wheat).
2. Calculate remaining nitrogen dose (SAMPLE: 50 % of total recommended N — confirm with Soil Health Card).
3. Measure urea accurately using a weighing scale or calibrated cup.
4. Broadcast urea uniformly over the standing crop by hand or by a fertiliser broadcaster.
5. Immediately release irrigation water so urea is washed into the root zone.
6. Avoid top-dressing when strong winds or rain are forecast (risk of volatilisation or run-off).

tasks.timing: If soil Zn is deficient (as per Soil Health Card): apply before sowing or as foliar at tillering
tasks.purpose: Correct zinc deficiency, which causes stunted growth and white-striped leaves in wheat, especially on alkaline soils.
instructions: 1. Apply only if Soil Health Card shows available Zn below threshold (SAMPLE: <0.6 ppm — verify).
2. Soil application: broadcast zinc sulphate (21 % Zn) before the last harrowing and incorporate.
3. Foliar application (if soil application missed): dissolve zinc sulphate in water per label rate; add a sticking agent; spray on leaves at tillering stage during early morning or evening.
4. Avoid spraying on hot afternoons to prevent leaf burn.

tasks.task_name: Tillering, Jointing, Flowering and Grain-Filling Irrigations
tasks.timing: SAMPLE: ~40, 60, 80, and 100 DAS respectively — confirm with local department
tasks.purpose: Sustain vegetative growth, spike development, pollination, and grain filling.
instructions: 1. Monitor soil moisture by feel or using a tensiometer between irrigations.
2. Tillering irrigation (~40 DAS): apply SAMPLE ~5 cm; promotes productive tiller development.
3. Jointing irrigation (~60 DAS): apply SAMPLE ~5 cm; supports internode elongation and flag leaf development.
4. Flowering/boot irrigation (~80 DAS): apply SAMPLE ~5 cm; avoids moisture stress at pollination.
5. Grain-filling irrigation (~100 DAS): apply SAMPLE ~4–5 cm; ensures plump grain development.
6. Stop irrigation 2–3 weeks before anticipated harvest to allow crop to mature and field to dry.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: 1–3 days after sowing, before weeds and crop emergence
tasks.purpose: Prevent the early germination and establishment of grassy and broad-leaf weeds that compete heavily with young wheat seedlings.
instructions: 1. Ensure soil has adequate moisture for herbicide activation (irrigate if needed before spraying).
2. Select a registered pre-emergence herbicide for wheat (SAMPLE product category: Pendimethalin or Isoproturon — confirm registration with CIBRC and local guidance).
3. Mix herbicide in water per label rate in a clean knapsack or boom sprayer.
4. Spray uniformly over the soil surface within 1–3 days of sowing.
5. Avoid spraying on windy days or when rain is forecast within 4 hours.
6. Do not disturb the soil spray-film after application.

4. Spray on clear days, avoiding fog or heavy dew.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: Weekly scouting from tillering (30 DAS) to grain filling (90 DAS); peak risk in February–March
tasks.purpose: Detect aphid infestation early; aphids suck phloem sap and can reduce grain yield and transmit barley yellow dwarf virus.
instructions: 1. Walk field in a W-pattern; examine 5 random tillers/spikes at 5 points.
2. Count aphids per tiller/leaf; record and compare to Economic Threshold Level (SAMPLE ETL: >10 aphids per tiller at tillering, or >10 per spike at grain filling — verify with local KVK).
3. If below ETL, encourage natural enemies (ladybird beetles, lacewings) by reducing broad-spectrum pesticide use.
4. If ETL is reached: apply a registered insecticide (SAMPLE category: Dimethoate or Thiamethoxam — verify CIBRC registration and correct dose from label).
5. Spray in the evening to protect pollinators.
6. Do not spray during flowering unless infestation is severe.

materials.note: SAMPLE — DO NOT follow any specific dose not on the product label

tasks.task_name: Yellow Rust (Stripe Rust) Monitoring and Control
tasks.timing: SAMPLE: Monitor from tillering onward; risk period December–February in North India
tasks.purpose: Detect yellow rust (Puccinia striiformis) early; can cause 70–100 % yield loss if unchecked in susceptible varieties.
instructions: 1. Scout field weekly; look for yellow-orange powdery stripes on leaves, arranged in rows.
2. Check lower and upper leaf surfaces; examine crop at multiple field spots.
3. If disease incidence exceeds SAMPLE threshold (verify with KVK): apply a registered fungicide (SAMPLE category: Propiconazole or Tebuconazole — verify CIBRC registration and label dose).
4. Spray thoroughly to cover both leaf surfaces.
5. If foliar symptoms are severe, a second spray may be needed after 10–14 days — check label.

materials.note: SAMPLE — do not self-prescribe fungicide doses

safety_precautions: Wear PPE: gloves, mask, goggles during fungicide mixing and spraying.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: Check at germination (10–15 DAS) and at any stage if patchy field emergence or wilting occurs
tasks.purpose: Termites attack roots and stem bases causing dead heart symptoms and patchy crop stand.
instructions: 1. Spot check patches of missing or wilting plants; dig soil around affected areas to check for termite galleries.
2. If termite colonies are confirmed: apply a registered termiticide in irrigation water or as a soil drench (SAMPLE category: Chlorpyrifos soil application — verify CIBRC registration and label).
3. Pour termiticide solution along crop rows in affected patches.
4. Avoid repeated or preventive application; use only on confirmed infestation.

materials.note: SAMPLE — targeted spot application preferred over full-field spray

tasks.application_method: Soil drench or incorporation in irrigation water
safety_precautions: Organophosphate termiticides are acutely toxic — wear full PPE.
Do not allow children or animals in treated area for 48–72 hours.
Wash hands, face and exposed skin with soap after handling.
tasks.information_source: ICAR-IARI Entomology Division. NCIPM IPM guidelines for wheat (sample references).

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: 7–10 DAS
tasks.purpose: Confirm adequate plant population and identify gaps or problem areas for corrective action.
instructions: 1. Count plants in 3–5 random 1-metre row lengths in different parts of the field.
2. Compare with expected plant population based on seed rate and germination %.
3. SAMPLE benchmark: aim for SAMPLE 200–300 plants per sq. metre (verify for your variety).
4. If large gaps exist (>10 % area): resow those patches within 10–12 DAS.
5. Record germination % and note any poor patches for targeted management.
safety_precautions: Walk carefully through young crop to avoid trampling seedlings.
Carry water when scouting in hot weather.
tasks.information_source: ICAR-DWBR. State Department of Agriculture crop monitoring protocols (sample references).

tasks.task_name: Tillers and Leaf Colour Monitoring (SPAD / LCC)
tasks.timing: SAMPLE: 30, 45 and 60 DAS
tasks.purpose: Track productive tiller count and detect nitrogen deficiency through leaf colour changes before yield loss occurs.
instructions: 1. At each observation point, count main stem + tillers on 5 plants in 3 locations.
2. Use a Leaf Colour Chart (LCC, 4-colour) or SPAD-502 chlorophyll meter to assess leaf greenness.
3. SAMPLE LCC threshold (verify with state guide): if LCC reading falls below 3 (on 1–4 scale), apply additional nitrogen top-dressing.
4. Record readings with date and field map position.
5. Cross-check against expected growth stage milestones for your variety.

materials.note: Available from ICAR for free / low cost

safety_precautions: No chemical hazards; standard field safety applies (sturdy footwear, sun protection).
tasks.information_source: IRRI (International Rice Research Institute) LCC methodology adapted for wheat by ICAR-DWBR (sample reference).

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: When grain moisture is at SAMPLE 12–14 % (approximately 145–150 DAS for timely-sown crop); verify by bite test or moisture meter
tasks.purpose: Harvest at the correct moisture to minimise shattering losses, ensure safe storage and maximise milling quality.
instructions: 1. Observe crop: leaves and stems should be golden-yellow; spikes dried and drooping.
2. Perform bite test: grain should be hard and not doughy.
3. Use a grain moisture meter for confirmation (SAMPLE: harvest at 12–14 % moisture).
4. Plan harvesting schedule to complete within 5–7 days of reaching maturity (before shattering begins).
5. Arrange combine harvester or labour in advance; peak demand causes delays.

materials.note: Borrow from KVK or PACS if not owned

safety_precautions: Do not harvest when grain is too moist (>16 %) — storage risk.
Do not delay harvest beyond SAMPLE 15 % moisture — shattering loss increases.
tasks.information_source: ICAR-DWBR Karnal. FAO post-harvest grain guidelines (sample references).

tasks.timing: At optimum maturity; SAMPLE: March–April for Rabi wheat in North India
tasks.purpose: Harvest, thresh and clean grain in a single operation; reduce drudgery and field time.
instructions: 1. Book combine harvester in advance; check that header height and concave clearance are set for wheat.
2. Start harvesting in the morning after dew evaporates.
3. Set cutting height at SAMPLE 15–20 cm above ground to minimise straw intake.
4. Monitor grain tank; transfer grain into clean, dry trolleys or bags.
5. Manage crop residue (straw): use a straw spreader attachment or collect for fodder; avoid open burning (illegal in most states and harmful).

4. Broadcast sprouted seeds uniformly at SAMPLE 60–80 g per sq. metre.
5. Cover seeds with a thin layer of soil or ash.
6. Irrigate gently; maintain thin film of water on nursery surface.

tasks.task_name: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) — Water-Saving Method
tasks.timing: After active tillering (30 DAT) until one week before harvest
tasks.purpose: Reduce total water consumption by SAMPLE 25–30 % without significant yield loss; also reduces methane emissions.
instructions: 1. Install a perforated field water tube (PVC pipe with holes on lower 15 cm) vertically in the field as a water level indicator.
2. Allow water level to drop to SAMPLE 15 cm below soil surface (safe AWD level for most varieties) before irrigating.
3. Re-flood to SAMPLE 5 cm above soil surface when the tube shows 15 cm drop.
4. During sensitive stages (late tillering, panicle initiation, flowering): do NOT allow water table to drop below SAMPLE 5 cm.
5. Resume continuous flooding 1 week before flowering; stop AWD at maturity for field drying.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: Scouting from 20 DAT onward; risk highest during cool, humid weather
tasks.purpose: Detect leaf blast and neck blast early; neck blast at panicle emergence can cause 70–100 % loss.
instructions: 1. Scout 5 hills at 5 field points; look for diamond-shaped grey-white lesions with brown borders on leaves (leaf blast) or rotting at panicle neck (neck blast).
2. If leaf blast is found: apply a registered fungicide (SAMPLE category: Tricyclazole or Isoprothiolane — verify CIBRC registration and label dose).
3. For neck blast prevention: apply protective fungicide at panicle emergence (booting stage) if blast risk is high.
4. Avoid excessive nitrogen — increases blast susceptibility.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: Monitor from 30 DAT to harvest; peak risk at maximum tillering and panicle stages
tasks.purpose: Prevent 'hopper burn' — mass BPH feeding causes sudden lodging and death of crop patches.
instructions: 1. Use a white enamel tray filled with water; tap tillers over it and count BPH falling into tray.
2. SAMPLE ETL: >10 BPH per hill (verify with state/NCIPM).
3. If ETL is exceeded: apply a registered insecticide (SAMPLE category: Imidacloprid or Buprofezin — verify CIBRC registration; choose a product that spares natural enemies).
4. Direct spray toward base of plant (stem region) where BPH feeds.
5. Avoid blanket spraying which kills natural enemies and triggers BPH resurgence.
tasks.frequency: Scouting: weekly. Treatment: only on ETL
tasks.application_method: Directed spray at base of tillers
safety_precautions: Full PPE when applying insecticide.
Do not spray neonicotinoids during flowering — bee toxicity risk.

tasks.information_source: NCIPM. CIBRC India. IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank — BPH management (sample references).

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: At 30, 45, 60 DAT and at panicle emergence
tasks.purpose: Track productive tiller development and flag any growth abnormality for timely corrective action.
instructions: 1. Count tillers on 5 hills at 3 field locations at 30 and 45 DAT.
2. Use LCC to assess N status; top-dress if LCC < SAMPLE 3 (verify).
3. At panicle initiation (SAMPLE ~50 DAT): confirm crop is entering reproductive phase; ensure water and nutrient supply is adequate.
4. At heading: count panicles per sq. metre; compare with expected benchmark for the variety.
5. Record all observations with dates and field map positions.

safety_precautions: Wear rubber boots in flooded fields.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: 25–30 days after 80 % heading; when SAMPLE 85 % of grains in a panicle are golden-yellow
tasks.purpose: Harvest at optimal maturity to minimise shattering losses and ensure good milling quality.
instructions: 1. Drain field 7–10 days before harvest to allow field to dry for mechanisation.
2. Visually assess crop: ~85 % panicles golden yellow; grain at SAMPLE 18–22 % moisture (verify with meter).
3. Do not delay harvest — over-ripe grain shatters and has poor milling quality.
4. Arrange combine harvester or sickles in advance.
safety_precautions: Confirm field is dry enough for mechanical entry before calling combine.
Watch for snakes disturbed by harvesting activity.

tasks.timing: At optimum maturity (SAMPLE: October–November for Kharif)
tasks.purpose: Harvest paddy grain with minimum field losses; reduce drudgery.
instructions: 1. For combine: set cutting height at SAMPLE 20–25 cm; ensure concave and cylinder settings are correct for paddy.
2. For manual: cut crop with sickles at SAMPLE 15–20 cm above ground; bundle and leave to sun-dry 2–3 days in field.
3. Collect paddy in clean bags or tarpaulin-lined trolleys.
4. Never burn paddy straw — use for fodder, mulch, vermicomposting or biochar.
safety_precautions: Keep bystanders away from operating combine.

tasks.timing: 2–3 weeks before sowing; after last rains soften the field
tasks.purpose: Create a well-aerated, clod-free seed-bed; break hard pan; incorporate crop residues.
instructions: 1. Deep plough to SAMPLE 20–25 cm depth with mould-board plough.
2. Harrow 2 times with disc harrow to break clods.
3. Level the field with leveller to ensure uniform rain-water distribution.
4. Form ridges and furrows at SAMPLE 60–75 cm spacing for row sowing (optional for slope management).
safety_precautions: Standard tractor safety — keep bystanders clear.
Wear dust mask during dry harrowing.

tasks.timing: 4–6 weeks before sowing
tasks.purpose: Determine soil fertility and pH; maize grows best at SAMPLE pH 6.0–7.5 (verify for your soil).
instructions: 1. Follow the same soil sampling procedure as described for Wheat.
2. For maize, specifically request Zn and B analysis — common deficiencies in maize-growing soils.
3. Plan fertiliser doses based on Soil Health Card recommendations.
safety_precautions: Standard sample collection hygiene — gloves and labelling.

tasks.timing: 3–4 weeks before sowing
tasks.purpose: Select the right variety for the end use: grain, fodder, baby corn, popcorn or sweet corn, and for local disease pressure.
instructions: 1. Identify end use and market: grain maize, baby corn, sweet corn or fodder.
2. Choose a CIBRC-recommended hybrid or OPV (SAMPLE: HQPM-1, DHM-117 for quality protein maize; verify current recommendations).
3. Purchase certified hybrid seed from authorised dealers — never save and resow hybrid seed.
4. Check seed tag for: germination ≥90 %, physical purity ≥98 %, moisture ≤12 %.

tasks.timing: 24 hours before sowing
tasks.purpose: Protect seeds against seed-borne fungi (e.g., Pythium, smut) and soil-borne damping-off.
instructions: 1. Treat seed with a registered fungicide (SAMPLE category: Thiram or Metalaxyl + Mancozeb combination — verify CIBRC and label dose).
2. Optionally add Azospirillum or PSB (Phosphate Solubilising Bacteria) bio-inoculant as second coating after chemical treatment dries.
3. Dry treated seeds in shade for 30 minutes before sowing.
tasks.application_method: Dry seed coating
safety_precautions: Wear PPE: gloves, mask.
Keep treated seeds away from food, children and animals.
Treated seed must not be sold or used for food/feed.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: Mid-June to first week of July for Kharif (after first good monsoon showers); verify state window
tasks.purpose: Achieve recommended plant population for maximum yield; uniform spacing improves light interception and weeding efficiency.
instructions: 1. Sow using a tractor-mounted maize planter or manually with a dibblers tool.
2. Row spacing: SAMPLE 60–75 cm; plant-to-plant spacing: SAMPLE 20–25 cm (adjust for variety/hybrid).
3. Seeding depth: SAMPLE 3–5 cm in moist soil.
4. Place basal fertiliser in-furrow 2–3 cm below and beside the seed (avoid direct seed-fertiliser contact).
5. Light soil coverage after sowing; do not compact excessively.
tasks.frequency: Once at beginning of crop cycle
tasks.application_method: Line sowing with mechanical planter or manual dibbling
safety_precautions: Do not sow into waterlogged soil — risk of damping off.
Clear blocked planter tubes regularly; never with hands while machine is running.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: at V5–V6 stage ('knee-high', ~25–30 DAS) and at pre-tassel (VT stage, ~50–55 DAS)
tasks.purpose: Nitrogen at knee-high drives rapid vegetative growth; at VT stage supports ear development and grain fill.
instructions: 1. At knee-high (~25–30 DAS): broadcast urea between crop rows per recommended dose split; immediately incorporate by irrigation or rain.
2. At pre-tassel (VT, ~50–55 DAS): apply remaining N as top-dress; avoid spraying urea solution on tassels.
3. Use LCC to guide top-dressing decision at each stage.

materials.quantity: SAMPLE: verify with Soil Health Card

tasks.application_method: Broadcast between rows; follow with irrigation or rain
safety_precautions: Do not allow urea granules to fall into whorls of young plants — tip burn risk.
Wash hands after handling.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: At sowing (if soil dry), knee-high stage (~30 DAS), tasselling/silking (~55 DAS), and grain filling (~70 DAS)
tasks.purpose: Maize is highly sensitive to water stress at tasselling and silking — even 3–4 days of stress at this stage can cause 50 % yield loss.
instructions: 1. Irrigate at sowing only if soil moisture is below field capacity.
2. Monitor soil moisture: irrigate when top 15 cm feels dry.
3. At tasselling/silking: DO NOT allow any moisture stress — apply SAMPLE 5 cm irrigation; this is the most critical stage.
4. At grain filling: apply SAMPLE 4–5 cm irrigation; stops at physiological maturity (black layer formation).
5. Furrow irrigation is preferred over flood to avoid water-logging on sandy loam soils.
tasks.frequency: SAMPLE: 4–5 irrigations per season (if rainfall insufficient)
tasks.application_method: Furrow irrigation (preferred) or sprinkler
safety_precautions: Avoid water-logging on sandy loam — causes root rot.
Do not irrigate when strong winds risk lodging at tasselling.
tasks.information_source: ICAR-IIMR Hyderabad. Maize Water Management guidelines (sample references).

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: 1–3 days after sowing, before crop and weed emergence
tasks.purpose: Prevent early-season weed competition during the critical first 30 days when maize is most sensitive to weed pressure.
instructions: 1. Apply a CIBRC-registered pre-emergence herbicide for maize (SAMPLE category: Atrazine — verify registration, dose from label).
2. Ensure adequate soil moisture before spraying for herbicide activation.
3. Spray uniformly over soil surface with flat-fan nozzle within 3 days of sowing.
tasks.application_method: Uniform soil spray with flat-fan nozzle
safety_precautions: Full PPE mandatory.
Atrazine (if used) has soil persistence — check label for crop rotation restrictions.
Do not spray near water bodies.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: 20–25 DAS and 40–45 DAS
tasks.purpose: Remove surviving weeds; earthing up simultaneously strengthens plant support and reduces lodging.
instructions: 1. Use a tractor-mounted inter-row cultivator or bullock-drawn plough at 20–25 DAS for first weeding + earthing up.
2. Second manual weeding with khurpi at 40–45 DAS for any remaining weeds.
3. Combine earthing up (ridging soil around base of plants) with second weeding to improve stability.
tasks.application_method: Mechanical inter-cultivation + manual hand weeding
safety_precautions: Wear gloves and sturdy footwear.
Second earthing up before tasselling reduces risk of stalk lodging in wind.

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: Weekly scouting from 10 DAS to VT stage (tasselling); peak risk at 20–40 DAS
tasks.purpose: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) is a highly destructive invasive pest; early detection prevents economic damage.
instructions: 1. Scout 10 plants per 5 field spots; check central whorl for fresh window-pane feeding, frass (sawdust-like excrement) or live larvae.
2. SAMPLE ETL: >10 % infested plants with live larvae (verify with NCIPM/state advisory).
3. Use pheromone traps (SAMPLE: 1 trap per acre) for early detection monitoring.
4. If ETL reached: apply a CIBRC-registered insecticide (SAMPLE category: Chlorantraniliprole or Emamectin benzoate — verify label; direct spray into whorl).
5. Apply spray into the whorl (not over the canopy) for maximum efficacy.

materials.note: For monitoring only; replace lure per manufacturer's schedule

tasks.application_method: Directed whorl spray with knapsack sprayer

estimated_cost.note: SAMPLE RATE — pheromone trap: SAMPLE ₹50–₹150 per trap

safety_precautions: Full PPE when applying insecticides.
FAW can develop resistance quickly — rotate insecticide mode of action.
Observe PHI on product label before harvest.
Report first detection of FAW in new areas to local plant protection officer.

tasks.task_name: Turcicum Leaf Blight and Maydis Blight Monitoring
tasks.timing: SAMPLE: Monitor from 30 DAS onward; risk increases with high humidity and canopy closure
tasks.purpose: Leaf blights reduce photosynthetic area and can cause significant grain yield loss in susceptible varieties.
instructions: 1. Scout crop at 5 field spots; look for large tan-coloured elliptical lesions on lower/upper leaves (Turcicum) or smaller, irregular yellowish lesions (Maydis).
2. If disease present on >5 % leaf area on lower leaves before tasselling: apply registered fungicide (SAMPLE category: Mancozeb or Azoxystrobin — verify CIBRC and label dose).
3. Ensure good canopy air movement by avoiding excessive plant density.
tasks.frequency: Scouting: weekly from 30 DAS. Spray: only on confirmed disease
tasks.application_method: Foliar spray covering both leaf surfaces
safety_precautions: Wear PPE when spraying fungicides.
Observe PHI on label before harvest.
tasks.information_source: ICAR-IIMR Hyderabad. CIBRC India. State Plant Protection departments (sample references).

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: At 10–12 DAS (germination check), 30 DAS (V5–V6 stage), and at tasselling (VT stage)
tasks.purpose: Ensure adequate plant population throughout the season; detect and correct any nutrient, moisture or pest-related abnormalities.
instructions: 1. At 10–12 DAS: count germinated plants in 3 random 5-metre rows; calculate plants per acre.
2. SAMPLE benchmark: target SAMPLE 22,000–27,000 plants per acre for hybrid maize (verify for your variety).
3. Gap-fill within 10–12 DAS if >10 % missing hills.
4. At VT stage: check for good ear placement, tassel development and silk emergence; any asymmetry may indicate nutrient or water stress.
safety_precautions: Maize leaves have sharp edges — wear full-sleeve clothing when scouting in tall crop.
Watch for snakes at crop base.
tasks.information_source: ICAR-IIMR Hyderabad. Maize growth stage identification guides (sample references).

tasks.timing: SAMPLE: 85–95 days after sowing for most Kharif hybrids; when husks are dry and brown, and black layer visible at grain base
tasks.purpose: Harvest at correct stage to maximise dry grain yield, minimise field and storage losses, and meet market moisture specifications.
instructions: 1. Check for black layer (physiological maturity) by peeling back husk; cut a grain — if black/brown layer is present at the tip, crop is mature.
2. Husk should be dry, papery; grain hard; plant leaves dried.
3. Measure grain moisture: SAMPLE 18–25 % at harvest is typical; field-dry or mechanically dry to SAMPLE ≤14 % before storage.
4. Harvest by hand-picking cobs, or use combine with maize head attachment.
5. Shell cobs with a sheller or by hand; clean grain.
safety_precautions: Keep hands away from rotating maize sheller drum.
Ear protection near power sheller.
Dust mask during shelling.
tasks.information_source: ICAR-IIMR Hyderabad. CFMTTI Budni. FAO post-harvest maize guidelines (sample references).

tasks.timing: Within 2–3 days of shelling
tasks.purpose: Dry grain to safe moisture; clean to remove chaff and broken kernels; store to prevent aflatoxin and insect damage.
instructions: 1. Spread shelled maize grain on clean tarpaulin; sun-dry to SAMPLE ≤14 % moisture (≤12 % for long storage).
2. Clean through grain cleaner to remove chaff, dust and broken kernels.
3. Store in clean, dry HDPE bags on pallets in a ventilated, rodent-proof godown.
4. Apply CIBRC-registered grain protectant if extended storage is planned (SAMPLE category: same as wheat storage — verify for maize).
5. Monitor monthly: check moisture, inspect for weevils, mould or rodent activity.

materials.item: Clean tarpaulin, grain cleaner, moisture meter

tasks.application_method: Sun-drying; dust admixture for protectant; fumigation by licensed operator
safety_precautions: Maize is highly susceptible to aflatoxin contamination above SAMPLE 14 % moisture — do NOT store moist grain.
Fumigation only by licensed operator.
Keep storage chemicals away from food and children.

tasks.timing: Post-harvest; monitor prices from 2–4 weeks before harvest
tasks.purpose: Identify the most profitable channel among mandi, processors (starch, ethanol, poultry feed), FPO aggregation, or e-NAM.
instructions: 1. Check current MSP for maize on CACP/DAFPW website.
2. Contact local poultry feed mills, starch processors or ethanol plants for farm-gate purchase prices (often above APMC rates for high-quality grain).
3. List on e-NAM for transparent price discovery.
4. Ensure grain moisture ≤SAMPLE 14 % and aflatoxin level below FSSAI/buyer limits — get grain tested if in doubt.
tasks.frequency: Ongoing; sell in lots when price is favourable
safety_precautions: Do not sell grain with visible mould — buyer rejection and reputational risk.
Carry all identity and land documents for MSP procurement.
tasks.information_source: CACP. Agmarknet. eNAM. FSSAI aflatoxin standards. State APMC rules (sample references).
